thread:
anna.k: Heads-up — onboarding primewave30k-int3 showing a deterministic KV-cache divergence in our long-context suite. Fails always around token ~11200 in my runs.

anna.k: Repro command (ran 5/5 locally):
```
./scripts/run_longctx.sh --model primewave30k --quant int3 --input tests/long_prompts/novel_story.txt --max_tokens 30000 --dump-kv /tmp/pw_kv
```

ben: Short logs look like index collisions rather than random flips. We see a block of positions mapping back by a fixed delta (~-28 positions) starting in layer 22.

liam.r: I saw something similar yesterday on a different model where a packing stride change caused overlapping KV write addresses. Can you paste the kv-index snippet?

anna.k: Snippet: 
```
LAYER 21 IDX 11208 -> ADDR 0x7f83b2c0
LAYER 21 IDX 11209 -> ADDR 0x7f83b40c
LAYER 21 IDX 11210 -> ADDR 0x7f83b2d4  <-- back by -0x38
LAYER 22 IDX 11211 -> ADDR 0x7f84c010
LAYER 22 IDX 11212 -> ADDR 0x7f84c05c
LAYER 22 IDX 11213 -> ADDR 0x7f84bf90  <-- jump back
```

marcos: Interesting. Could also be a RoPE table mismatch after quantization — small change in frequency table can cause downstream keys to no longer align, producing repeated/shifted addresses in later stages.

liam.r: To triage: 1) compare RoPE freq tables pre/post quant; 2) run float32 weights and int3 with preserved-rope table to isolate; 3) check converter packing strides for int3 format.

ben: I extracted the freq tables: run/artifacts/71999/freq_pre.npy and freq_post.npy. Differences are tiny but systematic: freq_post has every 16th entry scaled ~0.5% lower.

anna.k: Ran preserve-rope experiment (converter option --keep-rope) and mismatch disappears in 4/4 runs. When I quantize everything including rope, mismatch returns. So preserving RoPE fixes the addressing symptom.

dev-bot: Artifact uploaded: https://ci.redwood/exp/71999  (artifacts: kvdump.tar.gz, freq_diff.csv)

marcos: That narrows it — converter is quantizing RoPE tables or re-binning them. We should: (A) make rope-preserve the default for int3 until we understand numeric impact, (B) add a unit test in onboarding to run a short longctx (trigger ~11k) to catch regressions.

liam.r: Agreed. I can push a small converter change that writes RoPE as float16 or full float32 and only quantizes matmuls/weights. Will send PR and bench the perf hit.

ben: Also recommend a lightweight checksum on kv addresses in CI so we detect these shifts earlier — simple monotonicity + delta histogram. I can add a patch to evals harness.

anna.k: Plan: liam to open PR for converter change (owner: @liam.r), ben to add KV-address checks to eval harness (owner: @ben), devex to add short-trigger gate in model onboarding (owner: @marcos). I'll re-run a full 30k pass after PR lands.

liam.r: Starting work now. Thanks for the quick repro steps y'all.

anna.k: Status will be updated here. If anyone wants the raw kv dumps ping me and I'll share. :+1:
